chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said:
I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'The endive is a healing from a thousand illnesses. There is no illness in the inside of a son of Adam except that the endive suppresses it.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And one day he called for it for one of the servants, and the fever had seized him, and the headache. So he ordered that it should be pounded and rendered upon a paper, and the viola oil be poured over it, and for it to be placed upon his forehead. Then he said: 'But, it removes the fever and benefits from the headache, and eliminates it'.

key_terms.الْهِنْدَبَاءُ: Endive, a type of leafy vegetable known for its medicinal properties

ai.seo_question: What are the medicinal benefits of endive according to Imam Al-Reza (AS)?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating natural remedies with spiritual authority, presenting endive (al-hindaba') as a universal panacea that suppresses all diseases within the human body. The practical application—applying pounded endive mixed with violet oil to the forehead—demonstrates the Imam’s use of accessible, tangible treatments for common ailments like fever and headache, reinforcing the concept of 'Shifa' (healing) within the domestic sphere. This hadith is frequently cited in Shia medical jurisprudence to validate the efficacy of herbal medicine when endorsed by the Imams.
